I was told that I would not be allowed to do so without a hard inquiry into my credit. This would of course have a negative impact on my credit score. I also requested that they transfer the line of credit onto another of the cards that I have open with Citi, which was denied. I requested escalation and was connected to XXXX who is an Account Manager with ID # XXXX. She told the the same information. I have been a long-standing customer of Citi credit card and banking, and by having multiple card accounts across different financial institutions, I am aware as well that these practices -- the lack of notification and lack of remedy without a negative impact to the consumer -- are irregular within the industry, and are highly anti-consumer. Additionally, having an account closed by the company could reflect badly on credit reports and scores as well, both through the closure, as well as the reduction in outstanding credit in the debt/credit ratio. Citi knows I am a longstanding customer in excellent standing who has never failed to pay my obligations every month on time, and in fact still sees fit to extend me credit via other cards -- this decision had nothing to do with creditworthiness, just account activity. Therefore, I insist that the account be re-opened without a detrimental hard inquiry into my credit, or that I be allowed to transfer the full credit line to another Citi credit card account. Thank you for your consideration.
